"PROJECT: REALISTIC 3D BOXING SIMULATOR

1. GAME VISION

Create a highly detailed, realistic, physics-based 3D boxing simulation game inspired by the gameplay realism, movement systems, presentation, and fighting mechanics of Fight Night Champion and Undisputed.

The objective is to deliver an authentic professional boxing experience with lifelike human models, realistic boxing techniques, advanced physics, dynamic damage, character customization, career development, multiplayer competition, and immersive boxing environments.

The game should feel like controlling an actual professional boxer rather than an arcade fighting character.

Prioritize realism, responsiveness, tactical boxing, authentic animations, and physical interaction.

2. GRAPHICS AND CHARACTER MODELS

Create exceptionally detailed, photorealistic 3D human characters.

Requirements:

- Realistic human anatomy and proportions.
- Detailed facial structures and facial animations.
- Individual muscle groups that deform naturally during movement.
- Realistic skin textures, pores, wrinkles, sweat, bruising, and swelling.
- Physically accurate body movement.
- Natural muscle tension during punches and defensive movements.
- Realistic hand, wrist, shoulder, hip, and foot positioning.
- Accurate boxing gloves, hand wraps, shorts, shoes, mouthguards, and protective equipment.
- Realistic hair, facial hair, and customizable hairstyles.
- Different body types, heights, reaches, builds, and muscle distributions.
- Realistic aging and physical development.

Characters should look and move like actual athletes.

Use original fictional boxers with distinctive appearances inspired by the broad physical characteristics and boxing styles of real-world boxing archetypes. Do not reproduce protected identities, signature likenesses, branding, or official fighter assets without permission.

3. ADVANCED BOXING PHYSICS

The boxing system must use detailed physics-driven interactions.

Implement:

- Realistic punch trajectories.
- Momentum and weight transfer.
- Hip and shoulder rotation.
- Foot positioning and balance.
- Reach and distance calculations.
- Punch acceleration and deceleration.
- Punch resistance based on positioning.
- Collision detection between gloves and body parts.
- Impact reactions based on punch location and force.
- Body momentum and realistic recovery.
- Stamina-dependent punch speed.
- Fatigue-dependent movement.
- Realistic knockback and knockdown physics.
- Dynamic reactions when punches miss.
- Punches that can be interrupted or countered.
- Natural movement transitions.

Punches should not simply trigger canned animations. The animation and impact should respond to the fighter's positioning, movement, timing, stamina, and physical condition.

4. REALISTIC BOXING MOVEMENT

Include a complete boxing movement system.

Offensive movements

- Jab.
- Double jab.
- Power jab.
- Straight right and left.
- Cross.
- Lead and rear hooks.
- Body hooks.
- Uppercuts.
- Overhand punches.
- Short inside punches.
- Counterpunches.
- Combination punching.
- Clinch punches where permitted by the rules.

Defensive movements

- High guard.
- Low guard.
- Blocking.
- Parrying.
- Slipping left and right.
- Rolling under punches.
- Pull counters.
- Ducking.
- Leaning backward.
- Footwork-based evasion.
- Clinching.
- Lateral movement.
- Pivoting.
- Step backs.

Movement should reflect the fighter's weight, reach, conditioning, stance, and skill level.

5. REALISTIC DAMAGE AND FIGHT CONSEQUENCES

Implement a detailed damage simulation.

Different body regions should have independent damage and condition systems.

Head:

- Facial swelling.
- Bruising.
- Cuts.
- Nose damage.
- Eye swelling.
- Vision impairment.
- Blood effects.
- Concussion-related gameplay effects.

Body:

- Rib damage.
- Abdominal trauma.
- Body-shot fatigue.
- Reduced stamina.
- Reduced movement efficiency.

Arms:

- Arm fatigue.
- Reduced punching power.
- Defensive deterioration.

Damage should accumulate throughout the fight.

Blood and sweat should appear dynamically and react to lighting, movement, and impacts. Include adjustable visual violence settings.

Damage should influence fighter performance rather than being purely cosmetic.

6. CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION

Create a comprehensive boxer creation system.

Allow players to customize:

- Face shape.
- Eyes.
- Nose.
- Ears.
- Jawline.
- Skin tone.
- Hair.
- Facial hair.
- Height.
- Weight.
- Body composition.
- Muscle definition.
- Arm length.
- Reach.
- Shoulder width.
- Leg proportions.
- Tattoos.
- Scars.
- Boxing stance.
- Fighting style.

Include realistic body proportions and animations that adapt to customized characters.

7. BOXER DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION

Create a deep character development system.

Each boxer should have attributes including:

- Punch power.
- Punch speed.
- Accuracy.
- Hand speed.
- Head movement.
- Footwork.
- Defense.
- Blocking.
- Counterpunching.
- Chin durability.
- Body durability.
- Stamina.
- Recovery.
- Ring intelligence.
- Balance.
- Endurance.

Include:

- Training camps.
- Heavy bag training.
- Speed bag training.
- Shadowboxing.
- Sparring.
- Strength and conditioning.
- Roadwork.
- Reaction training.
- Technical coaching.
- Recovery and rest.
- Skill progression.
- Trainer relationships.

Attributes should improve through training and experience, with realistic limitations and diminishing returns.

8. CUTMAN MINIGAME

Between rounds, introduce a fully interactive cutman system.

The player should manage the fighter's physical condition during the one-minute break.

Include:

- Treating facial cuts.
- Reducing swelling.
- Applying ice.
- Using appropriate cut-treatment tools.
- Managing damaged areas.
- Wiping away blood and sweat.
- Communicating with the fighter.
- Managing limited treatment time.

The cutman's performance should influence the boxer's condition for the next round.

Make this a skill-based minigame with realistic animations and interactive mobile controls.

9. SPARRING MODE

Create a dedicated sparring environment.

Features:

- Headgear.
- Training gloves.
- Protective equipment.
- Adjustable sparring intensity.
- Different sparring partners.
- AI partners with different fighting styles.
- Practice specific punches.
- Defensive training.
- Combination drills.
- Counterpunch drills.
- Footwork training.
- Stamina management.

Sparring should be less damaging than professional competition.

Include the ability to pause, restart, and practice individual techniques.

10. GAME MODES

Career Mode

Start as an unknown amateur boxer and work toward becoming a world champion.

Include:

- Amateur competitions.
- Professional debut.
- Rankings.
- Fight contracts.
- Promoters.
- Trainers.
- Gyms.
- Training camps.
- Press conferences.
- Weigh-ins.
- Fight negotiations.
- Rivalries.
- Championship opportunities.
- Career statistics.
- Retirement.

Exhibition Mode

Choose any unlocked fighter and compete in customizable fights.

Multiplayer

Implement:

- Online ranked fights.
- Casual matches.
- Private matches.
- Invite friends.
- Custom tournaments.
- Weight-class matchmaking.
- Skill-based matchmaking.
- Global leaderboards.
- Player records.
- Online boxer customization.

Prioritize responsive networking, server-authoritative match validation, and fair competitive play.

Sparring Mode

Train against AI or another player without professional fight consequences.

Training Mode

Practice all punches, defensive techniques, combinations, and movement mechanics.

11. AI BOXING OPPONENTS

Create advanced AI opponents with different personalities and boxing styles.

Examples:

- Aggressive pressure fighter.
- Defensive counterpuncher.
- Technical outside boxer.
- Power puncher.
- Body-shot specialist.
- Fast combination puncher.
- Defensive specialist.
- Inside fighter.

AI should:

- Analyze distance.
- Manage stamina.
- Adapt to player tendencies.
- Use realistic combinations.
- Defend intelligently.
- Counter predictable attacks.
- Change strategies between rounds.
- Respond to damage and fatigue.

Opponents should have different levels of intelligence and technical ability.

12. REALISTIC BOXING VENUES

Create multiple lifelike environments.

Include:

- Major championship arenas.
- Small professional boxing venues.
- Underground boxing gyms.
- Amateur boxing halls.
- Outdoor boxing events.
- Historic boxing venues.
- Modern stadiums.
- Private training gyms.

Add:

- Realistic ring ropes.
- Canvas textures.
- Corner stools.
- Ring posts.
- Referees.
- Judges.
- Ring announcers.
- Photographers.
- Broadcast cameras.
- Crowd animations.
- Dynamic arena lighting.
- Crowd reactions.
- Walkout entrances.

Crowd atmosphere should respond dynamically to knockdowns, combinations, close rounds, and championship moments.

13. REALISTIC BOXING EQUIPMENT

Include detailed customization for:

- Boxing gloves.
- Hand wraps.
- Shorts.
- Boxing boots.
- Mouthguards.
- Headgear.
- Robes.
- Training clothing.
- Championship belts.
- Corner equipment.

Allow customization of colors, patterns, designs, logos, and materials.

Use original fictional brands and equipment designs unless licensed assets are available.

14. MOBILE CONTROLS

Design a complete touchscreen control system optimized for smartphones and tablets.

The controls must be responsive, customizable, and comfortable during long fights.

Suggested layout:

LEFT SIDE:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Forward movement.
- Backward movement.
- Lateral movement.
- Pivot controls.

RIGHT SIDE:

- Jab.
- Cross.
- Lead hook.
- Rear hook.
- Uppercut.
- Block.
- Dodge.
- Body/head targeting selector.

Additional controls:

- Stamina indicator.
- Health and damage indicators.
- Guard indicator.
- Lock-on or opponent tracking assistance.
- Combination input system.
- Context-sensitive clinch control.

Include:

- Customizable button positioning.
- Adjustable button sizes.
- Sensitivity settings.
- Left-handed layout.
- Optional gesture controls.
- Controller support.
- Haptic feedback.
- Accessibility options.

The interface must remain readable and usable on smaller phone screens.

15. CAMERA SYSTEM

Create a cinematic but gameplay-focused camera.

Include:

- Dynamic third-person boxing camera.
- Adjustable camera distance.
- Automatic opponent tracking.
- Smooth camera movement.
- Subtle impact camera effects.
- Knockdown cinematic sequences.
- Replay camera.
- Multiple viewing angles.
- Optional broadcast presentation.

Avoid excessive camera movement that interferes with competitive gameplay.

16. SOUND DESIGN

Implement realistic audio.

Include:

- Punch impact sounds.
- Glove-on-glove blocking sounds.
- Footsteps.
- Breathing.
- Grunting.
- Corner instructions.
- Referee dialogue.
- Bell sounds.
- Crowd noise.
- Ring announcer.
- Arena ambience.
- Walkout music using properly licensed or original compositions.

Audio should respond to fight intensity, fatigue, and damage.

17. REALISTIC MATCH PRESENTATION

Each fight should include:

- Fighter introductions.
- Walkout entrances.
- Ring announcements.
- Fighter inspection.
- Round announcements.
- Official scoring.
- Between-round corner interactions.
- Referee interactions.
- Knockdowns.
- Knockout sequences.
- Technical knockouts.
- Decision victories.
- Post-fight interviews.

Implement realistic boxing rules, weight classes, round lengths, scoring, fouls, and referee stoppages.

18. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

Build the game using a modern 3D game engine such as Unreal Engine 5 or Unity.

Priorities:

- High-quality character rendering.
- Realistic skeletal animation.
- Physics-driven character interactions.
- Inverse kinematics.
- Motion matching where appropriate.
- Procedural animation blending.
- Detailed hit detection.
- Optimized multiplayer networking.
- Scalable graphics settings.
- Mobile performance optimization.
- Efficient character and environment rendering.

Use high-quality assets on powerful devices and optimized models, textures, effects, and animation systems on mobile devices.

Target stable performance with adaptive graphics and scalable frame rates.

19. FINAL GAMEPLAY REQUIREMENT

The most important objective is to make every fight feel like a real boxing match.

Fighters must have weight, balance, momentum, vulnerability, fatigue, and individual fighting styles.

A player should need to understand distance, timing, defense, counterpunching, stamina, and positioning to succeed.

Avoid arcade-style combat, exaggerated movements, unrealistic flying punches, and repetitive canned animations.

The finished experience should combine the presentation quality of a professional boxing broadcast with the physical depth of a realistic combat simulator.

Create an original, commercially viable boxing franchise with its own identity, fighters, visual style, venues, and progression systems.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
